ea-gh-overcome-throne.reason: Opening section states the promise plainly (overcomers sit with Him in His throne), and later sections explain who overcomes and why, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-overcome-throne.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could the ones who overcome share Christ's own throne? Yes. Jesus promises it Himself: to him that overcometh, a seat with Him in His throne, even as He overcame and sat down with His Father (Revelation 3:21). Overcoming is not for spiritual superstars; it is faith in Jesus as the Son of Yahweh, holding on through trial. Here is what the Word says about that seat.
ea-gh-overcome-throne.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could the ones who overcome share Christ's own throne? They will, because He promised it. It is not a seat near the throne but with Him in it: family language for heirs and joint-heirs with Christ, adopted by the Spirit. The path is the one He walked first, and the victory that overcomes the world is our faith (1 John 5:4). The seat is given, never seized, and in Christ you are already raised up to sit together with Him (Ephesians 2:6). So each daily choice to trust, obey and endure is the family likeness showing on the road to that throne.

teen.open: Could people who overcome really sit on Jesus' throne with Him? Yes. Jesus promised it. Overcoming means trusting Him and holding on when life is hard.
teen.close: So the promise is real. Jesus overcame first, and He shares His throne with His family. Keep trusting Him; that is how overcomers live.

senior.open: The title asks whether overcomers could share Christ's throne. Revelation 3:21 answers yes, in His own words; and John defines the overcomer as the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of Yahweh.
senior.close: So the throne is the family's inheritance, given by adoption and not grasped. We walk the path He walked, overcome by faith, and endure today's trials as heirs.

ea-gh-door-sup.reason: First sections answer it (He knocks, never forces; the handle is on our side; open and He comes in to sup), but the lesson ends on discussion prompts, not on the invitation.
ea-gh-door-sup.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Revelation 3:20 say about being invited to supper with the King? That He stands at the door and knocks, but He does not force the lock; the handle is on your side. If you hear His voice and open, He comes in and eats with you, unhurried, like family. He said it first to a lukewarm church. Here is what that invitation means.
ea-gh-door-sup.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Revelation 3:20 say about supper with the King? That the King of kings, who could break any door, chooses to knock and wait, and when you open, He comes in to sup with you and you with Him. It is not only a once-in-a-lifetime knock. It is a daily question: is the door of your house, your schedule and your heart open, or has comfort kept Him outside? Open it. The table you share with Him today is a foretaste of the marriage supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9).

teen.open: What does Revelation 3:20 say? Jesus knocks on the door of your life. He will not force it open. If you open it, He comes in and eats with you like a friend.
teen.close: So the handle is on your side. Open the door to Jesus every day, and spend time with Him. It is supper with your best Friend.

senior.open: The title says the door has one handle, on our side. Revelation 3:20 shows the King knocking, not forcing, and promising table fellowship to any who hear His voice and open.
senior.close: So the knock is a daily invitation, even to believers. Open the door of house, schedule and heart, and enjoy now a foretaste of the marriage supper of the Lamb.

ea-gh-nothing-unclean.reason: The 'no' comes early, but the full answer (entry is by being written in the Lamb's book, washed in His Blood, not by our record) arrives mid-lesson; ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-nothing-unclean.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can anything impure ever get into heaven's City? No. Nothing that defiles, works abomination or makes a lie will ever enter it (Revelation 21:27). Yet we have all defiled and lied, so who gets in? Those written in the Lamb's book of life, whose robes are washed white in His Blood. Entrance is by the Lamb, not by our own clean record. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-nothing-unclean.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can anything impure ever get into heaven's City? Never. The gate condition is absolute, and the rebellion that once began in heaven will not get a second run in the new creation. That is good news, because it means a City that can never be corrupted again. And the way in is open to you: not how good am I, but is my name written in the Lamb's book? Trust the Lamb, not your record. Rejoice most that your name is written in heaven (Luke 10:20), and live like it now, purifying yourself as He is pure (1 John 3:3).

teen.open: Can anything bad ever get into Yahweh's holy City? No, nothing that lies or does evil. So how does anyone get in? Through Jesus, the Lamb, whose Blood washes us clean.
teen.close: So nothing impure gets in, and that keeps the City safe forever. Your way in is Jesus, not being perfect. If your name is in His book, live like it.

senior.open: The title asks whether anything impure can enter the holy City. Revelation 21:27 says nothing that defiles will enter, but those written in the Lamb's book of life will, having washed their robes in His Blood.
senior.close: So the City will never be corrupted again, and our place there rests on the Lamb, not our record. That hope moves us to purify ourselves now, as He is pure.

ea-gh-word-of-testimony.reason: How words become winning evidence (joined to the Blood, a testimony whose mouth and life match, aligned by eating the Word) is built across several middle sections; ends on prompts.
ea-gh-word-of-testimony.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could your own words be the evidence that wins? Yes, when they stand beside the Blood of the Lamb. The Blood answers every charge the accuser brings; your testimony agrees with it out loud. Words win when your mouth and your life run the same Word, so there is no gap to cross-examine. That alignment comes from eating the Word daily, as Jeremiah did (Jeremiah 15:16). Here is how it works.
ea-gh-word-of-testimony.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could your own words be the evidence that wins? They can, when they are joined to the Blood and backed by your life. The accuser lives on the gap between what we say and what we do. Eat the Word until it becomes the joy of your heart, and what you believe, say and live become one record. Then say so plainly, giving the credit to Yahweh first and to the people He used. That is a testimony the accuser cannot cross-examine, and the believers in Revelation overcame him exactly this way (Revelation 12:11).

teen.open: Can what you say help beat the enemy? Yes, when it stands with what Jesus did on the cross. Your words win when your life matches them, and that comes from feeding on Yahweh's Word.
teen.close: So stand on Jesus' Blood, feed on His Word every day, and tell what He has done for you. When your words and life match, the accuser has nothing to say.

senior.open: The title asks whether our own words could be the winning evidence. Revelation 12:11 joins the word of testimony to the Blood of the Lamb, and Jeremiah 15:16 shows how the Word, eaten, brings life and testimony into line.
senior.close: So the Blood is the ground and the testimony is its witness. When the Word eaten becomes the word spoken and the life lived, giving honour to Him, the accuser finds nothing to break.

ea-gh-judge-comes-with-reward.reason: Second section answers it (He carries a reward, not charges; the covenant turns His appearing into the family's payday), but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-judge-comes-with-reward.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does the Judge bring the reward in His hand? Because for His people He comes not with a list of charges but with payday: my reward is with me (Revelation 22:12). A crown is laid up for all who love His appearing. The covenant turns His coming from a courtroom summons into the family's payday, so you wait for Him with longing, not dread. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-judge-comes-with-reward.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the Judge bring the reward in His hand, and how does that change your waiting? Because He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him (Hebrews 11:6), and not one cup of cold water given in His name loses its reward. For those who belong to Him, the Judge is the Bridegroom, the King, the Friend. So you work like the reward is already in His hand, because it is. You keep the faith because the crown is laid up. And you wait as family looking toward the Father's house, praying with John, even so, come, Lord Jesus.

teen.open: Why is Jesus coming back with a reward? Because for His family, His return is payday, not a punishment. He sees every faithful thing you do.
teen.close: So you do not have to dread Jesus coming back. Keep being faithful, because your reward is already in His hand. You can say: come, Lord Jesus.

senior.open: The title says your payday is coming. Revelation 22:12 and 2 Timothy 4:8 show the Judge arriving with His reward, and a crown of righteousness laid up for all who love His appearing.
senior.close: So the covenant reframes judgment day: the Judge we honoured arrives as the Rewarder we loved. We labour faithfully, keep the faith, and wait with longing rather than dread.

ea-gh-yahweh-gets-both.reason: Opening sections answer it (credit needs having done it, worship needs worthiness; only Yahweh has both), and WHAT CHANGES restates it, but the lesson ends on discussion prompts.
ea-gh-yahweh-gets-both.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who earns worship? Only One. To deserve credit you must have done the work; to deserve worship you must be worthy in yourself. Yahweh alone has both: He created all things, and He is worthy (Revelation 4:11). Every other object of worship is itself a made thing. So exclusive devotion is not narrow; it is simply accurate. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-yahweh-gets-both.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who earns worship? Yahweh, and no one else can. He made heaven and earth and us, and He is worthy in Himself; the elders say both in one breath. That is why no other gods is not an arbitrary rule but a fact He is stating: anything else offered the position cannot hold it, and a soul built to rest on the Rock cracks on anything smaller. So your worship can rest on who He is, not on how you feel that morning. He made all things, and He is worthy. No one else can say both.

teen.open: Who deserves to be worshipped? Only Yahweh. He made everything, and He is perfectly good. Nothing else can claim both of those.
teen.close: So worshipping only Yahweh is not a narrow rule. It is just true. He made you, and He is worthy, so give Him your whole heart.

senior.open: The title asks who earns worship. Revelation 4:11 gives two reasons together: Yahweh is worthy, and He created all things. Nothing else in existence qualifies for both.
senior.close: So exclusive devotion is reasonable. It follows the fact rather than inventing a rule, and it gives worship a settled footing that does not rise and fall with feeling.

ea-gh-god-not-colorblind.reason: First section answers it (the redeemed stand before the throne with every nation and tongue named and kept, not erased), but the lesson ends on discussion prompts rather than the answer.
ea-gh-god-not-colorblind.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does Yahweh see your background or erase it? He sees it. In Revelation 5:9 the Lamb redeems people out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, and they stand before the throne still recognisably from each one. In Christ we share one standing and one song, but our stories are not flattened. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-god-not-colorblind.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does Yahweh see your background or erase it? He sees it, names it and keeps it. At Pentecost each person heard in his own language; before the throne every nation is still there, bought by the same Blood and singing one song. Equal standing in Christ does not mean the differences vanish, and seeing them is not favouritism, for He is no respecter of persons. So you are known before the throne in the whole of who you are, and you can see others the same way: honouring their story, weeping with them, and staying awake to how they are treated.

teen.open: Does Yahweh ignore where you come from? No. He sees your family, your language and your story. In heaven, people from every nation are still there, all singing to Jesus together.
teen.close: So Yahweh sees all of you and loves it. Everyone is equal in Jesus, and nobody's story gets erased. See other people that way too.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh sees our background or erases it. Revelation 5:9 answers that the Lamb redeemed people out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, with their distinctions named and kept before the throne.
senior.close: So we are one in standing and distinct in story. Heaven's way is recognised dignity, not pretended blindness, and it calls us to honour one another's background now.
